answer_text:
Let

\[
P_n=a_1a_2\cdots a_n.
\]

Since \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n\) converges, for any \(\varepsilon>0\) we can choose \(N\) such that

\[
\sum_{k=N}^{\infty} a_k<\varepsilon.
\]

For \(n\ge N\), split the product:

\[
P_n=(a_1a_2\cdots a_{N-1})\prod_{k=N}^n a_k.
\]

Set \(C_N=a_1a_2\cdots a_{N-1}\), a fixed positive constant. By AM-GM on the tail product,

\[
\left(\prod_{k=N}^n a_k\right)^{1/(n-N+1)}
\le \frac{1}{n-N+1}\sum_{k=N}^n a_k
\le \frac{\varepsilon}{n-N+1}.
\]

Thus

\[
P_n^{1/n}
\le C_N^{1/n}
\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{n-N+1}\right)^{(n-N+1)/n}.
\]

Multiplying by \(n\),

\[
nP_n^{1/n}
\le nC_N^{1/n}
\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{n-N+1}\right)^{(n-N+1)/n}.
\]

As \(n\to\infty\),

\[
C_N^{1/n}\to 1,\qquad
\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{n-N+1}\right)^{(n-N+1)/n}
\sim \frac{\varepsilon}{n},
\]

so

\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty} nP_n^{1/n}\le \varepsilon.
\]

Since \(\varepsilon>0\) was arbitrary,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n\sqrt[n]{a_1a_2\cdots a_n}=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]

27B·v4.method: AM-GM applied to the tail of the product (from index N onward), exploiting that the tail sum can be made arbitrarily small, forcing n·G_n ≤ ε for any ε.
